channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: That makes two full practices for the Chargers’ star wide receiver. Unless he suffers a setback, McConkey will suit up on Sunday to take on the Bills. He was on the field for 24-of-34 passing plays last week, and logged just six snaps outside of that. Hopefully, he can stay on the field for almost all of QB Justin Herbert’s dropbacks this week. McConkey should be in fantasy lineups.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chargers WR Brenen Thompson (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: The Chargers’ rookie speedster is on the wrong side of questionable. Thompson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but having him available is a plus for the offense overall. He will likely miss the Chargers’ Week 3 game against the Bills, though.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chargers LT Rashawn Slater (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: Chargers RG Cole Strange (pec) also upgraded to full participation today. Chargers G/T Trey Pipkins (knee) and LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) remained sidelined. Slate and Strange’s improvements are encouraging, but this unit is still in rough shape. Hopefully, everyone can remain setback-free.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Jones should be good to go for Week 3 against the Dolphins, but the calf injury is certainly limiting him. The Chiefs’ D/ST should have a good game, given the Dolphins’ offensive struggles.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Dolphins WR Chris Bell said he will play in Week 3 against the Chiefs despite being limited in practice by fluid and soreness in his knee.
item.description: Bell said the fluid and soreness have been bothering him since Week 1, but he has been pushing through it. The team is now limiting his practice reps so he can spend extra time working with the training staff. As far as how it impacts him, Bell said he has to spend more time warming up than he has in the past to avoid stiffness. Bell tore his ACL in November 2025. He is not yet running a full complement of routes and will likely remain on a snap count, at least in the short term.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saints WR Barion Brown (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: It seems like Brown is very unlikely to play at this point. His agility and long speed define his game as a gadget player and return specialist. His absence could benefit WR2 Devaughn Vele and WR Bryce Lance.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saints RB Kendre Miller (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Illnesses very rarely sideline players on game day, though this is worth tracking. Saints committee leader, RB Travis Etienne, remains limited by a hamstring injury. Saints RB2 Alvin Kamara could log a decent touch count this weekend against the Raiders, though he is a fairly inefficient player at this point.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Etienne remains limited, which keeps him in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 3 game against the Raiders. Saints RB3 Kendre Miller was sidelined by an illness, but those rarely impact NFL players’ availability on game day. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara should be rostered wherever he is available.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) remained limited on Thursday.
item.description: Meyers played through this thumb listing last week and was limited in back-to-back sessions to start the week; he should be considered likely to play against the Patriots.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) was limited on Thursday.
item.description: Hendrickson reportedly broke his finger “into several pieces” last week, yet still managed to record six quarterback pressures and one sack in Week 2. He should play again in Week 3 against the Cowboys in Brazil.-Nic Bodiford
